questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language of destination, the country and culture, courses at the university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, the host university was very good at giving us important information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy to apply for housing, but a very stressfull process to get a place to live. I only got my housing spot 1 week before arriving at my destination, which was very frustrating. Also, I got a space far from the university at an accommodation that i didn't initially apply for, even though there were spaces available closer to university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You cannot be certain to get a space at an accommodation you wished for, and you might get a response from the university about an available spot very close to the semester start. It can be a stressful process. 
When that is said, it is very nice and safe to live at a university accommodation and can be recommended. An easy way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The communication with the university was very helpful both before arriving and when registering upon arrival at the host university. They were very quick at replying to emails.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get assigned a student advisor at the host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I ended up not getting all the causes i wanted. This was due to the requirements at the host university and KU not matching. I ended up having to push one of my courses at KU and thereby finishing the bachelor in 7 rather than 6 semesters. 
However, the process of registering for courses at the host university was quite easy, and bit more challenging at KU.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient :)) you will suceed eventually

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one year 2 course, and two year 4 courses. The BA programe at University of Edinburgh is 4 years.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of self-studying, and often you only have one lecture a week in each course (and maybe one hour seminar class a week). Thereby you only have classes 6-8 hours a week when taking 3 courses, which is different from KU. You will come very good friends with the library. 
The teaching style is quite similar to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Health, Bodies and Embodiment 
Moral Psychology in the Real World 
Evidence and Enquiry: Research

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Health, Bodies and Embodiment was amazing, can definitely recommend. 
I took Evidence and Enquiry instead of Avanceret Forskningsdesign, which can thereby also be recommended.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Rent, very expensive. And public transportation (similar to Copenhagen).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh prices are quite similar to Copenhagen prices, maybe a bit cheaper. Be aware that rent i expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
University of Edinburgh have more than 300 societies, can definitely recommend being a member of a society. 
However, they don't really have any party societies like we have in KU (meaning no university parties...)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Yoga society, Hillwalking society, Sport society, Movie society etc. etc. Whichever society that you find interesting

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the highlands!!! - go on weekend trips, see more of the beautiful scottish nature and cities (Ilse of Skye, Inverness, Glencoe, Ben Nevis, St Andrews, Glasgow, Cairngorms national park etc.) 
And of course explore beautiful Edinburgh.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the scottish culture and people are amazing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Become a member of a society at the university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality and kindness of the scottish people, and their love for their country. (Bag pipes, kilts, tennents beer, pubs, rugby, cafes)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient with the process, it can take time and be challenging, but it is worth it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You might be disappointed with the courses or the exams, using your selective courses, or something else. But exchange is an experience that gives you so much more than studying. It is an experience for life, that you will never forget.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and getting friends from all over the world. Having a very special bond to the city (and country) you go to.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The application process

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
